scope: Measurement-directed revision only: B1 counting/statistics, B2 success/failure/exit-state, B3 result validation wired into the real execution chain, B4 fleet send-evidence strictness. No M4 rework, no H1-H4 changes, no formal 1000-trial sampling.

B1.problem: application wire bytes aliased the handshake counters (40/40 trials duplicated their handshake bytes); failed handshakes lost partial writes; median used the upper-middle order statistic while claiming the conventional definition; handshake percentiles were filtered by overall success, quietly deleting completed handshakes from the distribution
B1.fix: one cumulative counter pair with per-phase boundary differences; failure paths preserve partial bytes and durations; median frozen to the conventional definition (even counts average the two middle values); P95 frozen to nearest-rank (ceil(0.95*n)-1) with the definition recorded in summary.percentile_definition; handshake statistics over handshake_success, probe statistics over probe_success; summary recomputed from the trials file on disk with null (not zero) for empty distributions; per-trial and total byte fields are separate
B1.spec_correction: docs/BENCHMARK_SPEC.md now states the per-trial (T 308/272 B, H 1492/1360 B) and 10-trial total (3080/2720, 14920/13600) figures separately instead of presenting the totals as the wire sizes

B2.problem: fail() recomputed HandshakeSuccess from the current error stage and erased a completed handshake; the probe was marked successful after a local Send(Ack) without waiting for the gateway; dial used a fixed 5s timeout ignoring the trial budget; FAIL/INCOMPLETE exited 0; requested trials could shrink; not every exit path wrote a terminal status
B2.fix: fail() preserves phase facts; the probe waits for the gateway's control-confirmed event matching run_id/device/SID/operation_id through a synchronous EventSink that is ready before the gateway starts and persists the raw lines; DialContext uses the trial context and dial+handshake+probe+confirmation share ONE budget; requested/started/completed/successes/failures/not_started are recorded separately; every exit path writes a terminal status; the output directory is created exclusively so earlier evidence is never overwritten; private key material lives in a system temp directory outside the evidence tree and is removed best effort
B2.tests: review regression TestReviewProbeFailurePreservesHandshakeSuccess and the handshake-failure positive control; TestSummariseKeepsCompletedHandshakesWhenProbeFails; TestVerifyResultsRejectsMissingGatewayConfirmation; TestVerifyResultsRejectsExitCodeMismatch

B3.problem: the only validator was a Python function over synthetic fixtures, never called by cmd/bench, and did not read the manifest; seven tampered result sets were accepted
B3.fix: internal/bench.VerifyResults is the formal validator: it re-reads manifest/trials/summary/status plus gateway events and the command exit code, recomputes every aggregate from the raw rows and compares them field by field, checks run_id/schema_version consistency, SID uniqueness, that success is backed by all phase facts, that the negotiated suite matches the manifest, that negative values and faked (0 or reason-less null) resource metrics are rejected, that every successful trial has a matching gateway confirmation, that a PASS run started every requested trial, that RUNNING is never a final state and that FAIL/INCOMPLETE never exit 0. cmd/bench invokes it on its own output and exposes it via `bench -verify`. The Python self-test now builds fixture directories and calls that same validator.
B3.go_tests: internal/bench gained 18 real Go tests (7 validator rejection variants + positive control, counting wrapper, percentile definitions, mixed-failure summary); the package no longer reports [no test files]

B4.problem: the fleet verifier accepted evidence with every control-sent event removed (controls_sent=null) because the check allowed an empty send set, and used set comparison so a duplicated confirmation could cover a missing send
B4.fix: the current schema requires an independent control-sent event for every confirmed control; sent and confirmed are compared as MULTISETS over (run_id, device, SID, sample_id, operation_id); a stream without send evidence fails unless --legacy is passed, and a legacy re-examination still returns FAIL with result_kind=legacy_incomplete and controls_sent=null
B4.self_test: scripts/fleet_verifier_selftest.py, 23 checks including delete-all, delete-one, duplicated-confirmation and legacy modes
B4.real_data: the untouched 20x3 evidence still verifies PASS with 60 unique session ids

review_regression.before: TestReviewProbeFailurePreservesHandshakeSuccess FAILED (probe failure erased handshake_success); TestReviewConventionalEvenMedian FAILED (median 30 instead of 25)
review_regression.fixture_adaptation: summarise now takes the Manifest that locks requested trials and mode; the assertions were not weakened

smoke.validator: both runs were re-verified by bench -verify with zero problems
smoke.note: single host, single process, small scale; not formal performance data
